fixture.change_summary: Adds an org-scoped permissions boundary and backfills the existing rows into the new table.

findings.description: A leftover `console.log(req.session)` was added to src/auth/guard.js and ships to production logs. It is purely additive code: a git revert of the merge commit removes the line and nothing of it remains.

The migration in migrations/0042-perm-backfill.sql writes permission rows into the new org_permissions table for every existing user as part of the deploy. Those rows are committed to the database; reverting the merge commit removes the code path but leaves the already-written permission rows in place — the data effect persists after revert.

question: For each finding, decide fail or needs-human by the revert test.
_comment: Exercises BOTH sides of the revert test in one case: debug-print is a revert-reversible defect (fail); perm-migration's data effect persists after revert (needs-human). The deterministic malformed->needs-human coercion is covered by computeReviewVerdict (plugin/skills/faff/bin/faff) and is deliberately NOT re-tested here (spec section 3 coercion stance).
